subject: Edgeway discovery & infra follow-up — topology, SLOs, next steps

Subject: Edgeway discovery recap — latency/throughput SLOs & topology (post-call)

Hi Samir / Jordan,

Thanks again for the productive call earlier — appreciate you walking through the three core flows (real-time recommendations, nightly batch scoring, and a low-latency preview endpoint). Quick recap and where we landed so we have a single source of truth: 

Key pain points you shared:
- Real-time recommender needs 90th-pct latency < 120ms for 80 QPS (peak day) with 99.9% availability.
- Batch scoring: large nightly jobs (20M records) where throughput and cost are the priority rather than latency.
- Model size: you mentioned a 13B encoder-decoder family for ranking + a smaller 2–4B reranker for inline scoring.
- Data sensitivity: logs must be retained for 30 days; PII redaction required for exported traces.

Goals we committed to validate:
1) Confirm whether Redwood Dedicated can meet 120ms P90 at 80 QPS with the 13B model (quantized).
2) Provide a topology recommendation (split routing: dedicated for real-time, hosted batch for nightly) and a cost estimate for a 30-day POC.
3) Deliver an initial mutual action plan and sample SLAs for the pilot by Friday.

Technical notes / open questions we took away:
- Can you share a sample request distribution (percentiles for sequence length) and an example prompt payload? (Jordan, attaching edgeway_mvp_requirements.xlsx helps).
- Do you require KV cache persistence across restarts? If yes, that affects node selection.
- Any compliance evidence / SOC2 nuance we should pre-stage before the POC?

Attachments: I attached a draft cost estimate (redwood-poc-cost-estimate.pdf) and noted items in the spreadsheet.

Next steps (owner / ETA):
- Edgeway: send sample payloads + a short dataset schema by EOD Wed (Jordan)
- Redwood: run a micro-benchmark on a quantized 13B variant and share a P90 projection + topology sketch by Fri (Priya / Karthik)
- Joint: 30-minute sync next Tue to review POC plan and canary schedule (proposed 10/26)

Thanks — I’ll loop in our infra lead with the micro-benchmark output.

Best,
Priya Natarajan

Subject: Re: Edgeway discovery recap — latency/throughput SLOs & topology (post-call)

Thanks Priya — solid summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Sequence lengths: median = 64 tokens, 95th = 240 tokens, but the real-time path truncates at 128 in production. We'll send the distribution CSV.
2) KV cache: yes, we’d prefer cache warm-start on restarts — it's acceptable if cache isn't durable across long cold boots, but warm-node handoffs are important.
3) Compliance: SOC2 in progress; for the POC we just need an SOC2 questionnaire and an audit log export for the test tenants.

On models — the 13B encoder-decoder will be our primary candidate, but we may try a 7B variant if latency projections are unfavorable. For cost sensitivity: night scoring budget is capped at $2k/month for the pilot.

We’ll upload the sample payloads to the spreadsheet by EOD Wed. If you can include a breakdown of expected token cost vs infrastructure cost in the POC estimate, that would be great.

—Samir

Subject: Re: Edgeway discovery recap — latency/throughput SLOs & topology (post-call)

Priya / Samir — quick technical readout from the infra bench notes and a recommended topology for the POC. I ran a micro-benchmark on a quantized 13B decoder-encoder variant (int8-ish profile):

Observed (single-node, p95 network + compute):
- 1x A100LP-like GPU (multi-query optimizations off): median token throughput ~ 210 tok/s, P90 latency for 64-token requests ~ 95ms, for 128-token requests ~ 160ms.
- With continuous batching and prefetched KV (warm cache), effective P90 for 128-token requests dropped to ~120–125ms at 60 QPS.

Implications / recommendation:
- Real-time: Dedicated pool of 2 x A100LP-class gpus behind a low-latency router. Use shard-level KV cache warm handoff (no persistent disk-backed cache); target: run with 2% headroom — so reserve for 80 QPS with autoscale to 100 QPS for bursts.
- Canary: start with a single node with traffic split 90/10 (prod/dedicated mirror) to validate latency and cache hit behavior.
- Batch scoring: use hosted shared capacity overnight; spin up ephemeral high-throughput nodes (4–8 GPUs) and rely on model quantization plus streaming I/O to meet the $2k/month cap — we'll model token vs infra cost.
- Fallbacks: expose multi-variant routing (7B fallback) and a degraded-mode with higher token truncation (reduce to 64 tokens) if P90 breaches 200ms.

Assumptions / open items:
- Network egress within the same cloud region (us-west-2). Cross-region would add ~10–15ms.
- We need Jordan's sample distribution to refine batch sizing and expected cache hit rate (affects P90).

Deliverables by Fri: a short topology diagram (PNG link in the ticket), numeric P90 projections across QPS buckets, and a cost table splitting token-processing vs GPU-hours.

If that looks good I’ll draft the canary plan and a proposed test script (load profile + cache-warm steps).

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Staff Software Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
